solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mo's back!

definitions.meaning: a mo is a very short moment of time, as in 'wait a mo'
to back a motion or candidate is to support it formally

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone called Mo has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a brief instant of time (a mo), and the verb meaning to support a proposal.

clue.text: In Peel's day he mistreated a dozy kid?

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A man in the era of Sir Robert Peel abused a drowsy child.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel was the 19th-century Prime Minister who founded the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy, half-awake person, often affectionately a child, is called this.

clue.text: Primate's mischievous child overwhelmed by church

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overwhelmed by another sits beneath it, so the church comes first

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: An archbishop's naughty boy is overawed by the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, which fits 'church'; here it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimpanzee is one of the great apes, which belong to the primate order.

clue.text: Wicked US city accepting anything once!

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the city letters enclose the old word

parts.note: NY is New York
aught is an archaic word for anything

explanation.surface: A sinful American city that would once take anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty means badly behaved, and in older use was a stronger word for evil, so a near synonym.

clue.text: Sad endeavour to secure run for American singer

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or endeavour
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gloomy attempt to land a run for a US vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' suggests a human performer; here it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird of North America with blue plumage, so a feathered vocalist from that continent.

clue.text: Move suddenly east after a breather

indicators.note: in this down clue, the compass letter comes after the organ

parts.note: a lung is an organ one breathes with

explanation.surface: Dart eastwards once you have caught your breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' suggests a rest; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust of the body, so it means to move suddenly.

clue.text: Man in charge of army journal's last description of decree

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, the crossword's any-man
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: The editor of an army magazine describes a ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man in charge of' reads as one editor, but it splits into a man's name and the abbreviation for in charge. 'last' takes only the final letter of journal.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning relating to or of the nature of an edict, an official order.

clue.text: Lover upset a sailor of Arabian origin

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Omani means from Oman, on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A disturbed sweetheart: a seaman from Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a woman who is loved, used in English for a female sweetheart.

clue.text: Tabloid, possibly, not unknown in lower chamber

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a daily paper, of which a tabloid is one example
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A tabloid is no stranger to the lower house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish parliament's elected assembly is its lower legislative house.

clue.text: In the main it constitutes a seismic convulsion

definitions.text: In the main it constitutes a seismic convulsion

parts.words: In the main it constitutes a seismic convulsion
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is an earth tremor under the ocean

explanation.surface: Mostly, it amounts to an earth tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthquake whose epicentre lies under the ocean floor.

clue.text: Pie cooked by French priest, an enjoyer of good food

indicators.note: cooked in the sense of tampered with or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: curé is the French word for a parish priest

explanation.surface: A pie baked by a French cleric, who enjoys his food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' is the anagram signal, borrowed from the kitchen picture that 'Pie' sets up.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Epicurus, the word describes someone devoted to refined pleasures, especially fine eating and drinking.

clue.text: Arab artillery invading islands without question

indicators.note: invading means pushing into, so the gunners go inside the other letters
without in its old sense of outside, so the islands sit around the gunners and the query

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, so two of them give two letters
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Arab gunners storm islands, no questions asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without question' reads as 'certainly' but 'without' means outside: the two Is go round Q, and 'invading' puts RA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Arab nation of Iraq; the definition is a broader ethnic term the answer exemplifies.

clue.text: Propose article on music, meeting challenge

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: pop is a style of popular music
the definite article
to question something is to challenge it

explanation.surface: Suggest putting an article about music up against a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for asking someone to marry you, which is one specific sense of propose.

clue.text: Dispatch oxygen round Herts town, gradually increasing speed

indicators.note: round means the other letters go about the town

parts.note: to dispatch something is to send it
Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, an English county north of London
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Send oxygen around a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction from Italian telling players to press on faster little by little.

clue.text: Content, but extremely hazy about download?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer letters go round the other piece
extremely here means at the extremes, so only the outer letters of the word are used

parts.note: an app is a program one downloads to a phone

explanation.surface: Satisfied, though rather vague about something downloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Content as an adjective means satisfied or pleased, a close synonym.

clue.text: Well-known Republican feeding dog where otolaryngologists work

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the party letter goes into the dog

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian dog
these doctors work in ENT, the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A famous Republican feeds a dog at the ear, nose and throat clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent means important or famous, so widely recognized.

clue.text: Dutch painter left with worker, one making plea

parts.note: Karel Appel was a twentieth-century Dutch painter of the CoBrA group
a worker ant, the crossword's habitual worker

explanation.surface: A Dutch artist and a labourer, one of them pleading.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the party who lodges an appeal against a court's decision is making a plea to a higher court.

clue.text: Rich confections — the old man's samples

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa, with the possessive
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: Dad tastes sweet treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are sweet baked goods, often rich with butter and cream.

clue.text: Haughty nature of knight entering plant with sons

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these letters go into the plant

parts.note: aloe is a succulent plant
N is the chess notation for knight
S is the abbreviation for son, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: The superior air of a knight walking into a garden with his boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link here: it goes into ALOE along with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Being distant and standoffish is a haughty manner or disposition.

clue.text: Opera in which priest is bitten by dog?

indicators.note: bitten by means held in the jaws, so the dog's name goes around the priest

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a dog
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An opera where a clergyman is savaged by a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's only opera, the story of a wife rescuing her imprisoned husband.

clue.text: Bird identified by a good friend in Paris

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A bird spotted by a pal in the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The agami is a South American wading bird, also called the trumpeter.

clue.text: Spear produced by stupid person, say, leading to fine?

parts.note: an ass is a fool
eg, for example, is what 'say' means
A1 means first-rate, read as letters AI

explanation.surface: A spear made by a fool, leading to a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first class, is written with a one that stands for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The light throwing spear of southern African peoples, a particular kind of spear.

clue.text: Dodgy presentation of light sauce?

parts.note: a window is a light in a building, letting light in
a salad dressing is a kind of sauce

explanation.surface: A dubious display of some pale sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like an adjective for the sauce; it is a noun meaning a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a misleading display that makes something look better than it is, like a shop's arranged frontage.

clue.text: Excited cry over Lenin's first revolutionary device

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes before it

parts.note: whee is a cry of delight

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: A thrilled shout over Lenin's first revolutionary plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' with Lenin suggests politics; here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is a device that rotates, so it literally revolves.

clue.text: Bungling writer brought up in centre of Linlithgow

indicators.note: in means placed inside the middle letters
centre of means the middle two letters of the town's name
in a down clue, brought up means raised, so read bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: A clumsy author raised in the middle of a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Linlithgow is a town in West Lothian, Scotland; its centre is IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, so clumsy or bungling.

clue.text: Fellow US attorney visiting a medium

indicators.note: visiting means calling in, so the lawyer goes inside

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium, as on clothing
a DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A man and an American lawyer go to see a spiritualist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic; it is the size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man in Genesis, so a name used for any man or fellow.

clue.text: Live with wooded area around

indicators.note: around means the valley's letters surround the other one

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: A life spent beside a stretch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or have one's home there.

clue.text: English cleric backing new plant?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the clergyman's title is turned round

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric's title
green means new or inexperienced

explanation.surface: An English vicar supports a fresh plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is an example: not every plant keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree or shrub that keeps its foliage through winter is one kind of plant.

clue.text: Staid old lady, but about to relax at the front

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go round the initial pair

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
but in the sense of merely or just

indicators.note: at the front means only the opening letter of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A prim elderly woman is, however, on the point of unwinding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to relax' reads as 'going to unwind', but 'about' is the insertion signal and 'at the front' picks T and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the dignified, sedate manner of an older married woman, so a staid one.

clue.text: Back in resort, siblings find somewhere to eat

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are concealed within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Returning to a holiday town, brothers and sisters look for a place to have a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the signal for the concealed letters, so it is marked as such.
explanation.definitionFit: A small informal restaurant is a place where you go to eat.
